description.narrative: To have improved the status of the recipient water course of the River Neman and the Baltic Sea by enhancing the wastewater treatment in the City of Grodno to fulfil the HELCOM recommendations for municipal wastewater treatment.

This project was hampered by several issues related to the implementation of the reconstruction works. A contract with the Polish construction company Ecolog for the rehabilitation of the waste water treatment plant was initially signed in 2015. There were however many technical problems during the construction period, which ultimately led to a termination of the contract with Ecolog in June 2019. Thereafter much efforts were made by the project stakeholders to recoup financial resources from the failed contract and for the preparations for the re-tendering of a new main contractor.
Following a rather extensive re-tendering process a contract with a new main contractor, Shtang Construction Ltd (Israel), was signed in November 2020 with a planned completion by November 2022. The implementation of this contract was also very slow and the planned completion was extended several times. Following the suspension of the international financing to the project in the beginning of 2022, Shtang dismissed all personnel working on the project and left the object in the beginning of 2023.
In addition to the technical problems, this project was also severely affected by the political developments in Belarus and Russia. First came the contested presidential election in Belarus in August 2020, which was followed by harsh oppression of civilians voicing their discontempt with the election results. This ultimately led to Sida terminating all projects in Belarus involving the Belarusian state in July 2021. This also included the grant agreement with NIB regarding the project in Grodno. Due to the legal construction of this agreement, contracts that had been entered into by third parties could continue to receive disbursements of Sida funds until end 2022.
On 24 February 2022 Russia launched a military invasion of Ukraine, a campaign that was partly launched from Belarusian territory. This led to a formal suspension of NIB lending to Belarus on 14 March 2022.
These sad developments meant that Sida and NIB severed most contacts with Belarus and Grodno regarding the implementation of this project, which now means that the Belarusian partners will have to complete the project with their own resources. To facilitate this the PIU-consultant prepared a Roadmap to Actions after the suspension of the international finance.
